paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates training loss curves over iterations for multiple models. The x-axis is labeled "#Iteration" and spans from 0 to 140,000 iterations with regularly spaced tick labels every 20,000 iterations. The y-axis is labeled "Loss" and ranges from 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale, with regularly spaced tick labels every 0.1. A purple solid line with triangular markers represents the "Vanilla" model, starting at a loss value of approximately 3.4, decreasing to approximately 2.45 at 140,000 iterations. A cyan solid line with circular markers represents "StrmLLM (n=64)", beginning at a loss value of approximately 3.3 and decreasing to approximately 2.60 at 140,000 iterations. An orange solid line with square markers represents "SepLLM (n=64, H)", starting at a loss of approximately 3.3 and decreasing to approximately 2.51 at 140,000 iterations. A green solid line with diamond markers represents "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)", beginning at a loss value of approximately 3.3 and decreasing to approximately 2.49 at 140,000 iterations. A blue solid line with plus markers represents "SepLLM (n=128)", starting at a loss of approximately 3.3 and decreasing to approximately 2.55 at 140,000 iterations.
